extracted.intended_audience: IB Diploma Programme English A: Literature students and teachers (high-school)
extracted.subtask_short: IB DP English Literature written assignment
extracted.subtask_description: The official IB Diploma Programme rubric for the Language A: Literature written assignment, assessing the reflective statement and the written task across five formal criteria (A–E). Intended to guide marking of literary analysis/creative tasks and can be adapted to evaluate creative writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion A: Fulfilling the Requirements of the Reflective Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses how well the student shows their understanding of cultural and contextual elements developed through interactive oral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Level 1: Superficial development
Level 2: Some development
Level 3: Adequate development
Level 4: Substantial development
Level 5: Convincing development
(Assessors judge the degree to which cultural/contextual understanding derived from the interactive oral is developed in the reflective statement.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion B: Knowledge and Understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses depth of engagement with the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Level 1: Some knowledge but little understanding
Level 2: Knowledge and understanding with some insight
Level 3: Detailed knowledge and understanding with perceptive insight
Level 4: Excellent knowledge with persuasive insight
Level 5: Profound knowledge with original insight
(Focus on factual/textual knowledge plus analytical understanding and originality of insight.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion C: Appreciation of the Writer's Choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses how well student appreciates form, structure, technique, style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Level 1: Little appreciation
Level 2: Some appreciation
Level 3: Adequate appreciation
Level 4: Excellent appreciation
Level 5: Outstanding/insightful appreciation of how language, structure, technique, style shape meaning
(Evaluates sensitivity to literary craft and the student's ability to link choices to meaning.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion D: Organization and Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses essay structure, argument development, coherence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Level 1: Little organization or development
Level 5: Sophisticated structure that effectively develops insights
(Implicit intermediate levels 2–4 reflect increasing coherence, structure and development of argument.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion E: Language
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Level 1: Frequent inaccuracies; unclear
Level 2: (implied) limited clarity/accuracy
Level 3: (implied) generally clear and accurate
Level 4: (implied) clear, accurate, appropriate register
Level 5: Clear, varied, sophisticated; appropriate register; accurate vocabulary
(Evaluates correctness and stylistic quality of expression, including register and vocabulary choice.)

rubrics_metrics.name: IB aesthetic and evaluative priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-guidance: what the rubric's criteria collectively imply about IB's values in literature assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
- Form/structure/technique/style are constitutive of meaning, not decorative
- Originality of insight matters
- Cultural context is part of literary value
- Language quality (not just correctness) is criterial
(These points indicate that assessors expect analytical attention to craft, original interpretations grounded in context, and high-quality expression.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation as a Story-Quality Rubric
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested mapping of literary-analysis criteria to evaluate creative writing (story-quality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Mappings provided:
- Knowledge → Internal coherence of fictional world
- Appreciation → Successful deployment of form/structure/technique/style
- Organization → Story architecture
- Language → Diction, syntax, voice
(Useful guidance for repurposing the rubric to assess creative fiction rather than literary analysis.)
